title: Replacement resorption (ankylosis)
topic: Dead PDL after a long dry time: bone fuses to the root (ankylosis), then remodeling replaces the root with bone; no known arrest.

claims.claim: Replacement resorption: the root is gradually replaced by bone (title; crown and root filling remain in the drawing - schematic)
claims.source: AAE Glossary definition as quoted in Lin S, Moreinos D, Kaufman AY, Abbott PV. Dent Traumatol 2022;38:253-66 (PMID 35559593), Table 1 - review full text (research stage); Hammarstrom L, Blomlof L, Lindskog S. Endod Dent Traumatol 1989;5:163-75 (PMID 2517781) - abstract, monkey

claims.claim: DRY > 60 MIN - PDL cells likely non-viable; label PDL DEAD
claims.source: Fouad AF et al. (IADT avulsion guideline). Dent Traumatol 2020;36:331-42 (PMID 32460393), sect. 3 - guideline full text (research stage, AAPD reprint)

claims.claim: Bone grows across the dead PDL -> ANKYLOSIS (fusion shown before any root loss; source line says 'monkey')
claims.source: Andreasen JO, Kristerson L. Acta Odontol Scand 1981;39:1-13 (PMID 6943904) - abstract (authors' postulate: 'rapid osteogenesis in the alveolus which establishes an ankylosis'); order of events: Hammarstrom et al. 1989 (PMID 2517781) - abstract

claims.claim: Toy model / schematic: time strip WEEKS - MONTHS - YEARS and the shape/speed of the replacement front (labeled 'time scale schematic')
claims.source: Order of magnitude only: fusion at 1-2 weeks in monkey histology (PMID 2517781; Andreasen JO. Swed Dent J 1980;4:101-10, PMID 6933704); usually observed after 1-2 months in humans (Andreasen JO et al. Endod Dent Traumatol 1995;11:76-89, PMID 7641622) - abstracts

claims.claim: Root remodeled as bone (root replaced from the surface inward; front shape schematic)
claims.source: Andersson L et al. Int J Oral Surg 1984;13:423-31 (PMID 6438004) - abstract, background statement; Malmgren B. J Endod 2013;39(3 Suppl):S67-72 (PMID 23439048) - abstract, review

claims.claim: Age 8-16: root resorbed in 3-7 yr (>= 1 h dry; authors' conclusion from a radiographic index, mean follow-up 4.8 y)
claims.source: Andersson L, Bodin I, Sorensen S. Endod Dent Traumatol 1989;5:38-47 (PMID 2598883) - abstract

claims.claim: Signs: metallic percussion, no mobility, infraposition in a growing jaw
claims.source: Fouad et al. 2020 (PMID 32460393), sect. 11 - guideline full text (research stage); Kawanami M et al. Endod Dent Traumatol 1999;15:50-6 (PMID 10379271) - abstract; Campbell KM, Casas MJ, Kenny DJ. J Can Dent Assoc 2005;71:763-8 (PMID 16324230) - abstract

claims.claim: No known way to arrest it
claims.source: Campbell KM, Casas MJ, Kenny DJ. J Can Dent Assoc 2005;71:763-8 (PMID 16324230) - abstract ('no known treatment to arrest this condition'); Patel S et al. Int Endod J 2022;55 Suppl 4:892-921 (PMID 35229320) - review full text (research stage)

claims.claim: Growing patient: plan early, e.g. decoronation (inset: crown and root filling removed, root left to be replaced by bone - schematic)
claims.source: Malmgren B, Cvek M, Lundberg M, Frykholm A. Scand J Dent Res 1984;92:391-9 (PMID 6593804) - abstract; Fouad et al. 2020 (PMID 32460393), sect. 3.1.3 and 12 (decoronation is one listed option) - guideline full text (research stage)

claims.claim: Protect the PDL: replant at once, or store in milk (lowers the risk; not a guarantee)
claims.source: Fouad et al. 2020 (PMID 32460393), sect. 2-3 - guideline full text (research stage)

caption:
Replacement resorption: once the PDL dies, the root is remodeled like bone.
Dry > 60 min: PDL cells likely non-viable (IADT 2020). Bone bridges the dead PDL and fuses to the root (ankylosis; monkey histology), then the root is replaced by bone. Root canal treatment does not stop it.
Age 8-16, 1 h or more dry: root resorbed in 3-7 yr.
No known way to arrest it. Growing patient: plan early, e.g. decoronation.
Schematic animation.
Refs: Fouad 2020, Abbott & Lin 2022 Dent Traumatol; Andreasen & Kristerson 1981 Acta Odontol Scand; Andersson 1989 Endod Dent Traumatol; Campbell 2005 J Can Dent Assoc; Malmgren 1984 Scand J Dent Res
